land.text: Marrakesh and the south, captured in July 1668

predecessors.note: The Alawi page has 'Preceded by the Saadi dynasty'; the Saadi dynasty ended in 1659.

land.text: Fez (surrendered June 1666) and the Dila'iya domain in the north and the Middle Atlas (destroyed June 1668)

predecessors.note: A state Cliopatria lacks; it needs a dossier.
Forced to acknowledge al-Rashid's authority at a date the Alawi page does not give.

capitals.name: Tafilalt (Sijilmasa)
capitals.note: The page names no capital before Fez; the Tafilalt is the base of the Emir (1631-1666); coordinates are Sijilmasa's.

capitals.name: Meknes
capitals.note: Moulay Isma'il 'moved the capital from Fez to Meknes' during his reign (1672-1727); the page gives neither year, so both bounds are his reign's.

capitals.name: Fez (historical seat)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Royal Palace of Fez (historical)'; the page gives no capital dates after Meknes, so the span is a bridging reading; Abdelhafid signed the Treaty of Fez in 1912.

capitals.name: Rabat
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Rabat'; the page does not date the move and Rabat as seat under the protectorate is not on the pages opened, so it starts at independence.

rulers.name: Al-Rashid
rulers.note: Sultan of the Tafilalt 1664-1668, of Morocco 1668-1672.

rulers.name: Ahmad II (Abu'l Abbas Ahmad)
rulers.note: Two reigns, 1727-1728 and 1728-1729, with Abdalmalik in 1728.

rulers.name: Abdallah
rulers.note: Several reigns: 1729-1734, 1736, 1740-1741, 1741-1742, 1743-1747, 1748-1757, with other short reigns in between.

rulers.name: Yazid
rulers.note: Died in 1792 after a failed attack on Ceuta.

rulers.name: Abd al-Hafid
rulers.note: Abdicated after signing the Treaty of Fez on 30 March 1912.

rulers.name: Yusef
rulers.note: Proclaimed by the French on 13 August 1912.

rulers.name: Mohammed V
rulers.title: sultan, king from 1957
rulers.note: Deposed and exiled 1953-1955 (Corsica, Madagascar); Mohammed Ben Aarafa was installed by France 1953-1955; returned 16 November 1955.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Morocco row starts in 1670, but the Alawi page has the dynasty 'Founded 1631' and 'Mawlay al-Sharif was recognized as sultan of the Tafilalt in 1631'. The Alawi emirate is a principality around Sijilmasa until Fez surrenders in 1666 ('Emir (1631-1666)'); the page gives no boundary, so a radius around Sijilmasa is the researcher's reading. The Saadi Sultanate page (opened for the Saadi dossier, not counted here) says Abu Hassun reached Sijilmasa in 1631, so who held the Tafilalt that year is not settled.

correction.text: the Alawi principality in the Tafilalt around Sijilmasa, 1631-1665

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Al-Rashid secured the surrender of Fez in June 1666 and made it his capital' (the Alawi page); titles 'Emir (1631-1666), Sultan (1666-1957)'. Only Fez and the Tafilalt are named for 1666-1667; the rest of the Dila'iya north is taken in June 1668.

New keyframe: Al-Rashid 'destroyed the Dala'iyya capital in the Middle Atlas in June 1668 and captured Marrakesh in July 1668', so the sultanate holds all of Morocco from 1668, two years before Cliopatria's 1670 shape. Salé 'and its pirate republic' acknowledged him at an undated point.

correction.text: all of Morocco after Fez (1666), the Dala'iyya capital (June 1668) and Marrakesh (July 1668), as in Cliopatria's 1670 shape

keyframe_review.note: 384,192 km2: Morocco without the English Tangier (to 1684), Portuguese Mazagan (to 1769) and the Spanish places. The Alawi page says Moulay Isma'il 'retook coastal cities held by England and Spain' but names none and dates none, so no page opened dates the recaptures of Mamora, Larache or Asilah; if the shape already contains those Spanish places it overstates until their recapture. The infobox area (446,550 km2, modern) is not comparable for 1670.

384,893 km2, +701 km2 on 1686: Tangier. 'Morocco occupied the city on 7 February 1684' after the English had 'methodically destroyed the town and its port facilities'; the shape should take Tangier from 1684, three years before the Cliopatria shape starts.

correction.text: the shape unchanged, holding from 7 February 1684 (Tangier occupied)

keyframe_review.note: 385,343 km2, +450 km2 from 1741. No page opened dates anything in 1741; unverified: page budget. The Alawi page gives the 1727-1757 period as one of 'greatest turmoil' with short reigns.

387,614 km2, +2,271 km2 in 1769: Mazagan. 'The Kingdom of Portugal would continue to control the city until 1769'; Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah then took it over. The Alawi page's '1729' for Mazagan disagrees with the El Jadida page and is not followed.

387,443 km2, -171 km2 for 1842-1845, the years of the French Algerian shape's growth beside it. The Franco-Moroccan War page has the French occupy Oujda on 19 June 1844 and the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia (18 March 1845) fix a frontier 'from the Mediterranean coast to Teniet el-Sassi, some seventy miles inland'; no page explains a 1842 change, so unverified: page budget.

387,614 km2: the frontier of the 1845 treaty is in force: Yich and Figuig to Morocco, Ain Sefra, Sfissifa, Asla, Tiout, Chellala, El Bayadh and Boussemghoun to Algeria; the French 'refused to delineate the frontier to the south of Figuig', so the Saharan frontier stays undefined.

386,677 km2, -937 km2 from 1861: the Treaty of Wad-Ras (26 April 1860) 'retrocession' of Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena, 'ultimately identified as Ifni', to Spain, plus the Spanish sovereignty over Ceuta, Melilla and the Chafarinas it recognised. Spain held Tetouan 'until the reparations were paid'; the page gives no year for the withdrawal.
386,205 km2, -472 km2 and a lon-min change of 0.003 degrees: no page opened explains 1870; unverified: page budget.

358,263 km2, -28k km2 in the south-west (bbox south edge 27.93 -> 28.12 N, west edge 11.62 -> 11.33 W): this is the Tarfaya (Cape Juby) strip. The Spanish protectorate page treats the southern strip as part of the Spanish protectorate from 1912 and Morocco regained Tarfaya on 1 April 1958; no page opened dates 1885, so unverified: page budget.
358,422 km2: +159 km2; no page explains the change; unverified: page budget.

358,049 km2 to 1911. The Cliopatria row stops in 1911 and restarts in 1956: from the Treaty of Fez (30 March 1912) to 2 March 1956 the sultan reigned under French and Spanish protectorates and the Tangier zone (ledger 1912, 1956); the French zone is drawn as French Africa in Cliopatria, so no Moroccan keyframe is written for 1912-1955.

380,312 km2: independent Morocco after 2 March 1956 (French zone) and 7 April 1956 (Spanish zone), reunified with Tangier on 29 October 1956 (Tangier Protocol, Tangier page). Cliopatria's Tangier zone shape also runs to 1957. The shape is 85 percent of the infobox area (446,550 km2).
405,760 km2, +25,448 km2: Tarfaya, ceded by the Treaty of Angra de Cintra of 1 April 1958 after the Ifni War.
406,727 km2, +967 km2: Ifni, ceded by the treaty of 5 January 1969 ('The Spanish enclave of Ifni in the south was returned to Morocco in 1969', Morocco page).

406,464 km2 (-263 km2; unexplained): the shape stays Morocco's internationally recognised extent. Western Sahara is not in it; Morocco and Mauritania 'annexed' it in 1976 and Morocco 'controls and administers' about 70 percent of it (Western Sahara conflict page; the Morocco page says about two-thirds), so it is carried by the occupation event, not the shape.

406,464 km2 against the infobox's 446,550 km2 (the body says about 446,300): ratio 0.91, within the factor of two; the 40k difference is mostly the shape's coastline and the 1976 loss of 263 km2, the rest unexplained. Ceuta, Melilla and the other plazas de soberania are Spanish (Plazas page) and claimed by Morocco 'since its independence in 1956'.

region.text: the Tafilalt, where 'Mawlay al-Sharif was recognized as sultan'

ledger.note: 1631: Mawlay al-Sharif is recognised as sultan of the Tafilalt and the Alawi (Alaouite) state begins. 'Founded 1631'; the Morocco page's formation list gives 'Alawi 1631'. The Saadi Sultanate page (read for the Saadi dossier) has Abu Hassun in Sijilmasa the same year.
June 1666: Fez becomes the Alawi capital ('made it his capital').

region.text: Fez, whose surrender al-Rashid 'secured' in June 1666

ledger.note: June 1666: al-Rashid takes Fez. 'Al-Rashid secured the surrender of Fez in June 1666 and made it his capital.' The Alawi page does not name who held Fez; the Zawiya Dila'iya page (read for the Saadi dossier, not counted here) has the Dila'ites ruling central and northern Morocco until 1668 and the Alawites taking Fez first.

region.text: the Dila'iya domain: Fez, Meknes, the Gharb, the Rif plain, Salé and the Dala'iyya capital in the Middle Atlas, destroyed in June 1668

ledger.note: June 1668: al-Rashid destroys the Dala'iyya capital in the Middle Atlas. The page: 'He destroyed the Dala'iyya capital in the Middle Atlas in June 1668'; the Zawiya Dila'iya page (read for the Saadi dossier) says the Dila'ites ruled central and northern Morocco until 1668 when 'Dila' itself was annexed by the shurafa Alawites'. The extent is the researcher's reading; Salé and its pirate republic 'acknowledged his authority' at a date the page does not give.

region.text: Marrakesh, captured in July 1668

ledger.note: July 1668: al-Rashid captures Marrakesh and the Alawis hold all Morocco. The page: 'captured Marrakesh in July 1668'. The Saadi dynasty ended in 1659 (Saadi Sultanate page, read for the Saadi dossier); the pages do not say who held Marrakesh in between, hence 'nobody'.
1672: Moulay Isma'il, who reigned 1672-1727, moves the capital from Fez to Meknes. The page gives no year for the move; 1672 is his accession year (bridging).

region.text: Tangier, which 'Morocco occupied ... on 7 February 1684'

ledger.note: 7 February 1684: Morocco takes Tangier. Lord Dartmouth's forces 'methodically destroyed the town and its port facilities' for five months before Morocco occupied the city; the siege by Moulay Isma'il had been 'between 1678 and 1680 ... unsuccessful'.

region.text: Mazagan, the Portuguese 'last territory in Morocco'

ledger.note: 1769: Portugal abandons Mazagan and Sultan Mohammed ben Abdallah takes it over. 'The Kingdom of Portugal would continue to control the city until 1769'; most inhabitants were sent to Brazil. The Alawi page says Morocco took Mazagan in 1729, which the El Jadida page contradicts.

region.text: Oujda, which Marshal Bugeaud occupied after violating the frontier

ledger.note: 19 June 1844: Bugeaud occupies Oujda. The page: 'on 19 June 1844, Marshal Bugeaud violated the frontier and occupied Oujda'; the French fleet bombarded Tangier on 6 August and Mogador on 16 August and Bugeaud won at Isly on 14 August 1844.

region.text: the Algerian-Moroccan frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi

ledger.note: 18 March 1845: the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia fixes the frontier. 'from the Mediterranean coast to Teniet el-Sassi, some seventy miles inland'; Yich and Figuig to Morocco, Ain Sefra, Sfissifa, Asla, Tiout, Chellala, El Bayadh and Boussemghoun to Algeria; south of Figuig undefined. The Treaty of Tangier of 10 September 1844 had already ended the war.

region.text: the Islas Chafarinas, which 'Spanish troops conquered' in 1848

ledger.note: 1848: Spain conquers the Chafarinas Islands off the Mediterranean coast. 'In 1848, Spanish troops conquered the Islas Chafarinas'; Morocco recognised the sovereignty in the Treaty of Wad Ras (1860). The islands are smaller than one grid cell (region resolves to no cells; draw as a marker).

region.text: the Ceuta-Tetouan front

ledger.note: December 1859: the Spanish army opens the Tetouan campaign. The Cortes voted war on 22 October 1859; 'On December 17, hostilities were unleashed by the column commanded by Zabala' and O'Donnell landed at Ceuta on 21 December; the Spaniards entered Tetouan on 6 February 1860.

region.text: Tetouan, held by Spain 'until the reparations were paid'

ledger.note: 26 April 1860: the Treaty of Wad-Ras (the Peace of Tetouan) ends the war. Indemnity 20,000,000 duros, part funded by a British loan; Spain administered Tetouan until it was paid (the page gives no year for the withdrawal, so no occupation is drawn).

region.text: Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena, 'ultimately identified as Ifni'

ledger.note: 26 April 1860: Morocco cedes Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena to Spain for a fishing post. Its 'location was uncertain at the time and is ultimately identified as Ifni'; the Spanish protectorate page: Spain occupied Ifni in 1934 although it had been allocated to Spain by treaty since 1860. Ceuta, Melilla and the Chafarinas: Morocco 'recognizes Spanish sovereignty'. Counterpart spanish-empire, whose /ledger/104 records the 1860 Ifni gain from morocco (reviewer af-02-e).

region.text: Tangier, 'designated ... as an international zone'

ledger.note: 1912: Tangier is excluded from the protectorates. The Morocco page: 'In 1912 France and Spain designated Tangier as an international zone'; the Tangier page dates the convention 18 December 1923 and the Spanish protectorate page says the zone was set up in 1925, while Cliopatria's zone shape starts in 1912.

region.text: the French zone of the Treaty of Fez, the rest of the shape after the Spanish north

ledger.note: 30 March 1912: the Treaty of Fez makes Morocco a French protectorate. 'Abdelhafid abdicated after signing the Treaty of Fez on March 30, 1912'; the French proclaimed his brother Youssef sultan on 13 August 1912. Cliopatria draws the French zone as French Africa; the sultan reigned on.

region.text: the Spanish zone: 'a northern strip on the Mediterranean and the Strait of Gibraltar' and a southern part around Cape Juby

ledger.note: 27 November 1912: the Spanish protectorate in northern Morocco and the Cape Juby strip. The page's infobox gives 27 November 1912; capital Tetuan; about 20,000 km2. Tarfaya (Cape Juby) is already outside Cliopatria's 1885-1911 shape.

region.text: the French zone, after the Franco-Moroccan declaration of independence

ledger.note: 2 March 1956: France recognises Morocco's independence. 'The French-Moroccan Declaration of Independence was signed on March 2, 1956'; the Morocco page: 'Morocco regained its independence and reunified in 1956'.

region.text: the Spanish protectorate in the north, retroceded

ledger.note: 7 April 1956: Spain retrocedes the northern zone. 'Retrocession to Morocco: 7 April 1956', after France ended its protectorate.

region.text: Tangier, reintegrated by the Tangier Protocol

ledger.note: 29 October 1956: Tangier rejoins Morocco. Morocco reintegrated the city 'at the signing of the Tangier Protocol on 29 October 1956'.

1957: Mohammed V adopts the title of king and the sultanate becomes the Kingdom of Morocco. 'In 1957 he adopted the title "King."' (Titles: 'Sultan (1666-1957)' and 'King (1957-present)' on the page.)

region.text: Tarfaya, ceded by the Treaty of Angra de Cintra

ledger.note: 1 April 1958: Spain cedes the Tarfaya strip (Cape Juby). The page links the cession of the southern zone to the Treaty of Angra de Cintra 'dated 1 April 1958' and says Morocco 'gained Tarfaya in the Ifni War'.

region.text: Ifni, 'returned to Morocco in 1969'

ledger.note: 5 January 1969: Spain hands Ifni back. 'Morocco and Spain signed the treaty ceding Ifni on 5 January 1969' (Spanish protectorate page); the Morocco page: 'The Spanish enclave of Ifni in the south was returned to Morocco in 1969.'

region.text: the Spanish Sahara, which King Hassan's volunteers were asked to cross into

ledger.note: 6 November 1975: the Green March. 'On 6 November 1975, King Hassan asked for volunteers to cross into the Spanish Sahara'; Spain 'agreed to decolonise the territory' and, in 1975, to transfer it 'to joint Moroccan-Mauritanian control'.

region.text: the Spanish Sahara, annexed by Morocco and Mauritania in 1976

ledger.note: 1976: Spain leaves and Morocco and Mauritania annex the territory. The Western Sahara conflict page: 'both annexed Western Sahara in 1976'; it gives no date for the Spanish withdrawal.

region.text: Western Sahara, of which Morocco 'controls and administers' the part west of the sand wall (about two-thirds to 70 percent)

ledger.note: 27 February 1976: the Polisario proclaims the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic at Bir Lehlu and Morocco holds most of the territory. Morocco 'occupies about two-thirds of the territory' (Morocco page); the Polisario holds about 30 percent; the sand wall was built in six stages 1980-1987; Mauritania withdrew in 1979; ceasefire in 1991. No end: sovereignty is unresolved.

wars.name: Siege of Tangier (1678-1680)
wars.outcome: The siege 'between 1678 and 1680' failed; the English garrison destroyed the town and port and left, and Morocco occupied Tangier on 7 February 1684.
wars.note: The page does not say Khadir Ghailan led the siege; he was bound by a 1666 treaty until his death in 1673.

wars.name: Franco-Moroccan War

zones.text: Oujda and the frontier to Teniet el-Sassi

wars.outcome: France won at Isly on 14 August 1844; the Treaty of Tangier (10 September 1844) ended the war and the Treaty of Lalla Maghnia (18 March 1845) drew the frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi, leaving the south of Figuig undefined.
wars.note: The cause was Abd al-Kader's retreat into Morocco.

wars.name: Hispano-Moroccan War (1859-1860)

zones.text: Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena (Ifni)

wars.outcome: Spain entered Tetouan on 6 February 1860; the Treaty of Wad-Ras (26 April 1860) gave Spain Santa Cruz de la Mar Pequena (Ifni), recognised Spanish Ceuta, Melilla and the Chafarinas, and set an indemnity of 20,000,000 duros.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the Spanish withdrawal from Tetouan.

wars.name: Rif War

zones.text: the Rif and the Spanish zone

wars.outcome: The Rif Republic (1921-1926) 'was subdued by a joint Spanish and French expedition'.
wars.note: The sultanate under protectorate was not a belligerent; listed for the Rif border.

wars.name: Ifni War
wars.outcome: Morocco 'gained Tarfaya in the Ifni War'; the cession is dated by the Treaty of Angra de Cintra, 1 April 1958.
wars.note: The page gives no start year for the war.

wars.name: Sand War
wars.outcome: 'The Sand War was fought between Algerian and Moroccan troops' in 1963; the page gives no territorial result, so no zone and no contest event.
wars.note: The Alawi page traces the border disputes with Algeria to the French conquest of Algeria.

wars.name: Western Sahara War
wars.outcome: Morocco and Mauritania annexed the territory in 1976; the SADR was proclaimed on 27 February 1976; Mauritania withdrew in 1979; the sand wall was built 1980-1987; a ceasefire came in 1991 and sovereignty is unresolved, the Polisario holding about 30 percent.
wars.note: The Western Sahara conflict page gives no day for the ceasefire (6 September is not on it).

certainty.note: No treaty frontiers are on the pages: the Atlas, the Draa and the Saharan edge are approximate; Tangier and Mazagan, the Spanish and Portuguese places, are points.
The Algerian frontier from the Mediterranean to Teniet el-Sassi is sharp from the 18 March 1845 treaty; south of Figuig it is undefined. The Ceuta-Melilla enclaves are sharp from the 1860 treaty.
Treaty zones: the French protectorate of 30 March 1912, the Spanish protectorate of 27 November 1912 and the Tangier zone; the state itself has no drawn shape.
The Mediterranean enclaves and the Tangier and Spanish-zone limits are sharp; the Algerian frontier south of Figuig (Sand War 1963) and the Western Sahara line along the sand wall are not settled.

notes: Morocco (af-02-e). (1) Start: the Alawi page gives 'Founded 1631' (recognised sultan of the Tafilalt) while Cliopatria's row starts in 1670; three new keyframes cover 1631-1665 (Tafilalt), 1666-1667 (plus Fez) and 1668-1669 (all Morocco). Cliopatria's Saadi rows 1670-1740 (652.8 km2) are marked wrong in the Saadi dossier. (2) 1912-1955: Cliopatria has no Morocco shape; the French zone is drawn as French Africa (its shape covers 349k km2 of Morocco in 1912, 1930 and 1953, the years checked), Tangier as the Tangier International Zone. The sultan reigned under the protectorates (rulers listed), so the state is dormant on the map rather than ended: the ledger records the three 1912 losses and the three 1956 gains. Under rule 4 the protectorate should be a vassal tint of France and Spain; the af-08 French Africa dossier should decide that; no keyframe is written for 1912-1955. (3) Pages silent or dateless: Moulay Isma'il's recapture of Mamora, Larache and Asilah (Alawi page: coastal cities from England and Spain, undated; Tangier is dated by the Tangier page), Salé's submission, the Spanish withdrawal from Tetouan (the HM page: after the indemnity, no year), the 1885 loss of the Tarfaya strip, the Algerian frontier changes 1912-1972, the Madrid Accords day, the 1979 transfer of Oued Ed-Dahab from Mauritania, and the Tetouan occupation. (4) Disagreements: the Alawi page puts Mazagan in 1729, the El Jadida page in 1769 (followed); the Tangier zone is 1912 (Morocco page and Cliopatria), 1923-24 (Tangier page) or 1925 (Spanish protectorate page); Marrakesh June/July 1668 versus Cliopatria 1670. (5) Western Sahara: the shape does not include it (Cliopatria excludes it); the 1976 occupation event hatches it with the SADR as owner; Mauritania's share until 1979 and the Moroccan share west of the wall are not split by the pages. (6) New states needed: dila-iya-sultanate, bou-regreg-republic, sahrawi-arab-democratic-republic, rif-republic (counterparts_needing_dossiers); Spanish Sahara as a colony is under francoist-spain in Cliopatria's terms. (7) Gazetteer names lacking (radius used): Mazagan is covered by 'El Jadida'; Ifni, Tarfaya, the Chafarinas, Touat are not named; 'Tafilalt' region resolves to a much larger area than the Alawi principality, so a radius around Sijilmasa is used. The Morocco infobox 446,550 km2 includes the claimed area.
